facts.label: Reagir e mostrar interesse
facts.sub: Use sounds + adjetivo (That sounds fun) e sounds like + substantivo ou frase (It sounds like a good plan). Com I, you e they, use sound sem s.

facts.label: parece + adjetivo
facts.sub: Use That sounds + adjetivo para reagir: That sounds interesting, fun, great. Depois de sounds vem o adjetivo, nunca well. Com I, you e they, use sound sem s: You sound happy.

facts.label: parece que…
facts.sub: Use It sounds like + substantivo ou frase: It sounds like a perfect place. It sounds like you’ll enjoy it. Depois de like você pode usar uma ideia completa.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “parece interessante” ou “que legal”, com o verbo parecer.
compare.us: Em inglês, use sound + adjetivo: That sounds interesting. Para substantivo ou frase completa, use sounds like: It sounds like a good plan.

items.s: Sounds + adjective is a common reaction.
It sounds like a great idea uses sounds like.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.

answers: Sounds + adjective is a common reaction. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “That sounds well.” → Falso (We say That sounds good.)
It sounds like a great idea uses sounds like. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A café in Portland · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy evening in a café in Portland. Dario and Sara sit by the window with hot tea. Dario has a new hobby, and he is excited. Sara listens and asks many questions. The café smells like coffee and fresh bread. A friend’s story can sound like an adventure.

“Sara, I started a small garden on my roof last month. I grow herbs.” says Dario. “That sounds interesting! Do you get enough sun up there?” says Sara. “Yes, it’s sunny all day. Next week I’m going to add a bench.” says Dario.
